items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I experienced playing with Shadow Wilson, which I felt like was one of the greatest drummers I'd ever played with.

ctx.x: But anyway, sometimes, like I said, somebody's misfortune is your good fortune.. And I needed a job, and the fact was, I talked to him about it, and it wasn't a thing that he was regretful about it, because he wasn't going back with Illinois. So I had no guilt about taking anybody's job. Anyway, I was with the band, and I stayed with the band from January to September.
I experienced playing with Shadow Wilson, which I felt like was one of the greatest drummers I'd ever played with.

As I said before every now and then, you play with a musician that just has something that touches you, and Shadow Wilson was one of those people who was just an excellent player. You couldn't play in a band with Shadow Wilson and be sluggish or lag behind, because he had a way, if you were what he called "shuckin'", he'd hit the drums and tell you to come on! You're lagging!
